note: Custom Tokens defines two entity types: token_custom (translatable content entity, base table token_custom; fields name, machine_name, type[bundle], description, content[text_long value+format]) and token_custom_type (config bundle entity, config name token_custom.type.<machineName>; default type 'custom' ships in config/install). Tokens resolve as [<type>:<machine_name>] via hook_token_info + hook_tokens using getFormattedContent()=check_markup(value,format), guarded by the cached allowlist token_custom.allowlist. Managed at /admin/structure/token-custom (configure route entity.token_custom.collection). Permissions: administer custom tokens, administer custom token types, access custom tokens overview. No Drush, no plugin types. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real entities: introspection reads back an existing token/type; execution creates a token (and a token type) and is verified by actually replacing the token via \Drupal::token().

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal token_custom (Custom Tokens) module, if I create a custom token with machine name 'company_name' under the default token type, what token string do I use to output it, and where do I create it in the admin UI?
evals.expected_output: Use [custom:company_name] (the default token type is 'custom'). Create it at Administration > Structure > Custom tokens (/admin/structure/token-custom) via 'Add Token', choosing the token type and entering the machine name and content.

evals.prompt: What two entity types does the token_custom module define, and which one is a configuration bundle? What default token type ships with the module?
evals.expected_output: token_custom is a content entity (each token); token_custom_type is a config bundle entity grouping tokens into types. The default token type that ships in config/install is 'custom' (so tokens are [custom:...]).

evals.prompt: Which permissions does token_custom provide for controlling who can manage custom tokens and token types?
evals.expected_output: Three permissions: 'administer custom tokens' (create/edit/delete tokens, restricted), 'administer custom token types' (manage token types, restricted), and 'access custom tokens overview' (view the overview page).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has one custom token defined with the token_custom module. Inspect the live site and tell me the token's machine name and the text it outputs.
evals.expected_output: The token is tc_greeting (type 'custom'); its content is 'Welcome to Example Co', so [custom:tc_greeting] outputs that text.

evals.prompt: Besides the default 'custom' token type, a custom token TYPE has been created on this site with the token_custom module. Inspect the live configuration and give the machine name of that additional token type.
evals.expected_output: The additional custom token type is tc_promo (config entity token_custom.type.tc_promo), alongside the default 'custom' type.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the token_custom module to create a custom token with machine name 'tc_task' under the default 'custom' token type, whose content is exactly the text: Support ticket resolved. Apply it to the live site so that [custom:tc_task] resolves to that text.
evals.expected_output: A token_custom entity with machine_name tc_task, bundle 'custom', content value 'Support ticket resolved' exists (e.g. via the Add Token form or TokenCustom::create([...])->save()), so \Drupal::token()->replace('[custom:tc_task]') returns text containing 'Support ticket resolved'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the token_custom module to create a NEW custom token type with machine name 'tc_dept' (label Department), then create a custom token with machine name 'tc_manager' under that new type whose content is exactly: Jane Doe. Apply it to the live site so [tc_dept:tc_manager] resolves to that text.
evals.expected_output: A token_custom_type config entity 'tc_dept' (token_custom.type.tc_dept) exists, and a token_custom entity 'tc_manager' with bundle tc_dept and content 'Jane Doe' exists, so \Drupal::token()->replace('[tc_dept:tc_manager]') returns text containing 'Jane Doe'.
